Announcement
HRF Grants $500,000 to 14 Projects Worldwide
Written by
Human Rights Foundation

NEW YORK  (March 19th, 2024) — The Human Rights Foundation (HRF) is pleased to announce its Q1 2024 round of gifts from its   Bitcoin Development Fund  . HRF’s latest batch of grants focus on global education, Lightning Network development, decentralized communications, and providing nonprofits and human rights groups with an easier onramp to financial freedom tools. Areas of focus include Latin America, Asia, and Africa.
Grants include:

• USD E-Cash for Bitcoin by   Calle  , a USD-based Chaumian e-cash system built on the   Cashu   protocol. This system would enable private, affordable, and stable use of USD-denominated credits, all interoperable with the broader Bitcoin Lightning network. USD E-Cash is positioned as an alternative to major stablecoins, in that it does not have any connection to the traditional banking system. The core idea is that activists anywhere can exchange their bitcoin for privacy-protecting dollar-denominated E-Cash, with the trade-off of being custodial. Funding will support the full development of this project.

•   BTCPay Server  , a free, open-source, self-hosted payment solution that enables individuals and businesses to accept Bitcoin payments. BTCPay provides a platform for merchants in difficult political and economic climates to process global payments, manage crowdfunding campaigns, and offers developers opportunities to kickstart their projects on top of Bitcoin. Funding for BTCPay Server will support UI/UX improvements, feature enhancements, contributor rewards, and training programs.

•   BOB Builders Residency Program  , an in-person residency for Free and Open-Source Software (FOSS) developers located in Thailand. The new cohort of developers will focus on “Toolings to Reinforce Bitcoin’s Decentralization,” to combat centralizing forces in the software ecosystem. The previous cohort, also supported by HRF, focused on privacy. Funds will be used to support the residents of this second cohort, covering living and travel expenses.

•   Yibaochina.com   议报中文, a popular news platform led by   Citizen Power Initiatives for China  , serves Chinese scholars, intellects, and writers abroad. Dedicated to promoting democracy, human rights, and the rule of law in the global Chinese-speaking community, Yibao has gained a significant readership, particularly in pro-democracy communities within China. HRF’s grant will support the wages of writers, editors, and translators of the site, as well as social media promotion efforts, as they translate Bitcoin educational materials and news items into Chinese for wide circulation into the world’s biggest dictatorship.

•   Bitcoin Innovation Hub  , a physical space and community center promoting the socioeconomic transformation of refugees, asylum seekers, and other vulnerable communities led by   Noble Nyangoma   in Kampala, Uganda. The hub offers a range of vocational training and financial literacy to women and men in various fields, where they learn how to use and how to earn Bitcoin, regardless of what kind of ID they hold. Funding will support the addition of vocational classes (ie. digital skills, carpentry, and baking) for thousands of students in the East African region, enabling stateless communities to earn Bitcoin for their work.

•   BITCOIN DADA  , a non-profit initiative founded by Kenyan entrepreneur   Lorraine Marcel  , aims to empower African women through financial education. BITCOIN DADA provides a safe space for women to learn about Bitcoin as a tool for financial freedom and build up their skill set. Funds will support the expansion across Africa, the creation of multilingual educational resources, and promote women-led businesses adopting Bitcoin. The grants in this round to Bitcoin DADA and to the Bitcoin Innovation Hub are generously supported by Strike’s nonprofit initiative.

•   The Bitcoin Design Foundation   exists to support the Bitcoin Design Community, which is dedicated to providing design infrastructure and resources to bitcoin designers and developers, including those building for people living under authoritarian regimes and in developing economies. The funding will support the development of the Bitcoin UI Kit (a resource that help people learn, design, prototype, and build full bitcoin applications) as well as the addition of new and emerging techniques for privacy and self-sovereignty in the Bitcoin Design Guide. Improving the UX of Bitcoin wallets remains a top goal.

•   Bitcoin Op-Tech  , a technical Bitcoin newsletter renowned for its industry-leading resources, technologies, and techniques tailored for Bitcoin developers, businesses, and organizations. The newsletter regularly covers issues of privacy, censorship-resistance, and decentralization which are core to HRF’s mission. Additionally, Bitcoin Op-Tech offers workshops, documentation, original research, and case studies. Funds will be allocated towards operational expenses and growth strategies.

•   Damus Android  , a communications application using the nostr protocol. Developed by   Will Casarin  , Damus ensures free speech online — critical for people living in difficult political environments without being censored — and enables users to receive Bitcoin through its “zapping” functionality. Funding will be used to develop the Damus application for Android devices, helping to potentially onboard millions of new users in authoritarian countries and the developing world.

• Bitcoin Core Developer   Pablo Martin  , whose initial work addressed a vulnerability that caused a Bitcoin node to crash and shut down. Martin continues to contribute, review, and put forth proposals advancing Bitcoin, including the http-rest interface, bitcoin-cli, p2p, rpc, and the wallet within the Bitcoin repository, while also contributing to Bitcoin Core GUI repositories. Funds will support his ongoing contributions to Bitcoin development, the likes of which are crucial to keeping Bitcoin a secure tool for activists everywhere.

•   LNbits  , a multi-user and account system for the Lightning Network, enables users to create separate Lightning wallets for friends and family. Built by software developer   Ben Arc  , LNbits aims to decentralize custodianship and provides users with a robust suite of Bitcoin tools they can run for themselves, for others, or as part of a stack. Funding will support the core contributors’ salaries, bounties, and educational outreach efforts through workshops and video tutorials.

•   Bitcoin Policy Summit 2024  , a one-day conference bringing together policymakers, academics, and industry leaders to explore the opportunities and challenges of Bitcoin. The event aims to reshape the narrative surrounding Bitcoin, advocate for its benefits in liberal democracies, and highlight its potential to undermine closed societies. Funding will support event logistics, speaker travel, and attendance by human rights advocates.

• Bitcoin for Billions, a series of informative videos created by Bitcoin educator,   Paco de la India  . The videos, initially available in four regional languages — Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, and Gujarati — aim to have a wide audience among the 750 million people in India who speak these languages. Topics include the concept of bitcoin as freedom money and practical guidance on purchasing and self-custodying bitcoin safely, items which are increasingly important under a regime that continues to trend more authoritarian. The grant will be used for research, content creation, translation, and promotion of the videos.

•   Scalar School  , founded by   Luciana Ferreira  , a Brazil-based Bitcoin and Lightning development program dedicated to training early-stage Bitcoin developers. The school equips students with a comprehensive understanding of Bitcoin development, philosophy, and community engagement, preparing them for future opportunities in esteemed programs such as Chaincode Labs. The grant will go towards teachers’ salaries, training workshops, and university outreach and will give a boost towards developers living in South America.

Alliance is the world's most selective accelerator & founder community.            $400k Funding  Interview invites sent within 1 week of application. Immediate funding upon admission.           Apply to    by  November 18     Apply          “The community is amazing. We love it.   We created so many meaningful relationships with the smartest builders in the space.  Alliance also helped us – both highly technical engineers – turn Zerion into a much better product".         Evgeny Yurtaev, Zerion                       “Instrumental for our success, has increased our progress by over tenfold.   Mentors are extremely generous with their time and are able to introduce us to almost anyone we need.  Working with them was the best decision we've ever made as a startup".         Morris Hsieh, Primodium                       “An incredibly well-run program.   Alliance has been a massive value-add to us across all business functions, including go-to-market, strategy and recruiting.  Highly recommend to all founders”.         Matthew Katz, Caldera                                   Our Startups                                              Join our Community   Graduate from the accelerator to join our select community of 700+ crypto & fintech founders.                Balaji Srinivasan  Angel Investor         Kain Warwick  Founder of Synthetix         Kevin Lin  Co-Founder of Twitch         Lenny Rachisky  Angel Investor         Prasanna Sankar  Founder of Rippling         Siqi Chen  CEO at Runway         Charles Naut  Co-Founder of Rain              Our Program  2-week in-person onboarding followed by an 8-week fully remote program for global participants.                                        WEEK 1 - 2  New York City, United States      Meet the Cohort   Start developing the relationships with peers and mentors that you'll leverage during acceleration and beyond. While challenging, this process will help you hone your product's pitch and vision.         WEEK 10  New York City, United States      Demo Day   Present your product to leading VCs, angels & experts. Receive exclusive media coverage.       Graduation   Demo Day presenters become Alliance DAO members – joining the most exclusive crypto & fintech founder community. Fortune              Seismic raises $10M led by a16z crypto to bring confidential computing to fintech          TechCrunch              Tensor raises $3M for Solana-focused NFT trading platform          Fortune              Exclusive: DeFi platform Azura launches after raising $6.9M from Initialized          The Block              Rain raises $6M led by Lightspeed to launch stablecoin-powered corporate cards          The Block              Ex-Revolut duo raise $6 million seed round to expand onchain finance app Bleap            How to Apply                          Frequently Asked Questions       Who should apply?            If you're a technical founder building something ambitious, you should apply. Don't overthink it.  We've backed teams across every stage and vertical – crypto, AI, fintech, stablecoins, and more. Pre-product, pre-revenue, mid-pivot, anything goes.  Some of our biggest successes applied before they had anything built. Others had already raised funding before Alliance. There's no perfect formula.  The only thing we care about: you want to build something big and your team can ship.  The application takes about 20 minutes. You'll get a response faster than any other accelerator.  If you're debating whether to apply, that's your answer. Just apply.        Who should NOT apply to Alliance?            Historically, four types of founders have struggled at Alliance:      Founders optimizing for a short-term outcome or quick flip.  Our founders are building for the long term – generational companies that will be remembered decades from now. If the idea of selling your startup tomorrow for $20 million sounds enticing, you're not operating on the same timeframe as Alliance.      Founders building a lifestyle business.  Nothing wrong with that path, but Alliance is built for venture-scale outcomes and our pace reflects it.     Founders looking for funding alone.  While we provide initial capital, we are NOT investors. Our value comes through mentorship and community. If you're just looking for a check, there are much better options out there.     Founders who crack under pressure.  Alliance means check-ins every single week, hard feedback from mentors, building in public, and an extreme degree of accountability. The program is intense by design. You may need to fire your entire team, move countries, restart from scratch and pivot multiple times – not everyone has the stomach for it.      We're upfront about these failure modes so applicants can self-select out and avoid wasting their time.  If, however, reading this list made you even more excited, you're exactly the type of founder who should apply.        Should I apply if I haven't built a product yet? What if I don't have any traction?            Yes. Some of our most successful startups applied before they had anything built – no MVP, no traction, no revenue. We care far more about the founder than the product.        Should non-crypto-native or Web2.5 startups apply?            Yes. We've always backed startups with varying degrees of crypto involvement – including fintechs, payment APIs, SaaS for crypto startups, AI products and more.  We view startups as existing along a spectrum within crypto. Some are deeply crypto-native, while others are less so. We don’t mind where you fall on that spectrum.  Our mission is to partner with the most exceptional founders in the world – regardless of the specific product you're building today.        When should I apply?            We run 3 cohorts a year. For each cohort, there's both an “Early Admission” and a “Regular” deadline.  We strongly encourage teams to submit applications as early as possible, as it maximizes your chances of selection.  Since most teams apply close to the deadline, applying early gives us much more time to review your application.        When does the program start?            ALL19, our next cohort, starts on January 11, 2027.        The next cohort start date is too far away.            We make interview decisions within 1 week of receiving an application, all year round. Once you’re accepted, we start working with you right away.  The official cohort start dates are mainly for logistical purposes and have minimal impact on your actual acceleration experience.        How much does the program cost?            Nothing, the program is entirely free.  We only require a $400k investment in your company (at unparalleled, founder-friendly terms). We've learned that our best performing teams actually do want us to have skin-in-the-game. And our investment further aligns us with your success.  Besides this, founders' only obligation is to ensure they have the time and energy to attend sessions and work with mentors. We expect full commitment during the program's 3 months.        My startup has no plans to launch a token. Should I still apply?            Yes. Most Alliance startups never launch a token.  The 1:1 token side letter is standard for all investments and simply means that if you ever do launch one, Alliance as your investor would have a claim to it. It doesn't create any constraints on your business.        Does Alliance support founders who require visas or immigration assistance?            Yes – we’ve supported many founders in navigating immigration and visa-related challenges as part of our program.  Admission to Alliance is recognized as strong evidence of “extraordinary ability,” which can be an important factor in visa applications such as the O-1.  We also work with experienced immigration attorneys and advisors, and can connect you to trusted legal resources. While final decisions rest with the relevant authorities, most Alliance founders who required visas have successfully secured them with support from our network.        Does the program provide funding?            Yes, we offer $400k in funding to all admitted startups.  Alliance invests at a $4M post-money valuation via SAFE with a 1:1 token side letter.        I have received better funding offers. Why join Alliance?            Most founders we admit had offers at better terms and chose Alliance anyway.  That's because Alliance isn't funding. We're not investors. Capital is the least useful thing you get.  The real value is mentorship from partners and our founder community.        I need funding now, I can't wait for next cohort. What should I do?            If you'd like to take advantage of Alliance's funding but your fundraise timeline doesn't match the next cohort, don't worry. We've often supported startups by funding them  before  they're accelerated.  Just submit your application as you normally would. We review applications all year long and will invite you to an early interview if your startup meets Alliance's criteria.        Does Alliance offer perks and discounts?            Yes, Alliance has in place over 90 deals for our founders.  These include credits at Anthropic, AWS, Google Cloud, Gemini, Notion, Mercury, OpenAI, Privy and many other key services.  You can expect these credits to save your startup hundreds of thousands of dollars for costs you'd incur regardless.        If accepted, when will I receive funding?            Once you’re accepted into the program, we immediately start the investment and KYC process. For most teams, this takes less than a week.  After paperwork is signed, KYC is completed, and payment details are verified, we wire funds. This typically takes 1 to 2 weeks and happens before the program starts.        How is the program structured?            The program relies on 4 core activities: lectures, 1:1 mentorship, weekly check-ins and Demo Day.      Lectures:  We run weekly sessions where successful founders from our community share their stories and learnings as crypto operators, followed by a Q&A.      1:1 Mentorship:  Startups receive 1:1 mentorship from Alliance mentors. Discussions often revolve around product, go-to-market and fundraising. At times, mentors may also intro founders to experts within our network depending on the problem at hand.     Weekly Check-ins:  Founders share accomplishments and challenges with mentors every week to maintain accountability, momentum and gain insight on how to overcome potential blockers.     Demo Day:  6 weeks into the program companies start working on their narrative and pitch. Then, on week 10, startups meet select angels and VCs at Demo Day – both in-person, at the Alliance HQ in NYC, and online – and graduate from the program.      Each startup in our latest cohort received an average of over 50 intro requests after Demo Day from crypto's most value-add angels or funds, such as Paradigm, Multicoin and Dragonfly. Most startups also receive significant interest from clients or potential partners.        How is Alliance different from other accelerators?            The best people to answer this are founders who've done other programs before Alliance. Here's what they consistently tell us:     Cohorts are deliberately small (15-30 teams), which means mentors are truly hands-on. We get into the details of your product, your GTM, and your fundraise with you, everyday.    The peer support is something most founders say they didn't expect, but it ends up being one of the most valuable parts of Alliance.    And because we've been in the space since 2020, we're often one intro away from the exact customer, partner, or investor you need.         What are the next steps after I submit my application?            After you apply to the program, mentors will review your application within 1 week.  Our team will then invite ad hoc the most promising teams for an interview over Zoom. This will consist of a 10 minute fast-paced conversation with Alliance mentors (with guidelines shared before the interview).  Final decisions are then communicated over email within 24 to 48 hours.  Note that due to the sheer number of applications and interviews, mentors are unfortunately not able to give personalized feedback to teams that are not selected. You've seen Cursor sell to Elon for $60B . Maybe the previous generation was Mark Zuckerberg or Evan Spiegel. You look at these founders and compare yourself to them. They don't seem that much smarter than you. Their resumes aren't better than yours.      Imran Khan · Jun 18           Yamanaka Factors: How Four Proteins Could Rewind Aging    For most of the last century, biologists treated aging the way a mechanic treats an old car. Parts wear out, damage piles up, and the slow rusting eventually stops the engine. Under this view, aging runs in one direction. Biology has no reverse gear.      Qiao Wang · Jun 2           Finding Unlikely Allies    When Founders build on top of someone else's platform, they can activate a network of allies they could never have afforded to recruit. It doesn't create any constraints on your business.        Does Alliance support founders who require visas or immigration assistance?            Yes – we’ve supported many founders in navigating immigration and visa-related challenges as part of our program.  Admission to Alliance is recognized as strong evidence of “extraordinary ability,” which can be an important factor in visa applications such as the O-1.  We also work with experienced immigration attorneys and advisors, and can connect you to trusted legal resources. While final decisions rest with the relevant authorities, most Alliance founders who required visas have successfully secured them with support from our network.        Does the program provide funding?            Yes, we offer $400k in funding to all admitted startups.  Alliance invests at a $4M post-money valuation via SAFE with a 1:1 token side letter.        I need funding now, I can't wait for next cohort. What should I do?            If you'd like to take advantage of Alliance's funding but your fundraise timeline doesn't match the next cohort, don't worry. We've often supported startups by funding them  before  they're accelerated.  Just submit your application as you normally would. We review applications all year long and will invite you to an early interview if your startup meets Alliance's criteria.        Does Alliance offer perks and discounts?            Yes, Alliance has in place over 90 deals for our founders.  These include credits at Anthropic, AWS, Google Cloud, Gemini, Notion, Mercury, OpenAI, Privy and many other key services.  You can expect these credits to save your startup hundreds of thousands of dollars for costs you'd incur regardless.        If accepted, when will I receive funding?            Once you’re accepted into the program, we immediately start the investment and KYC process. For most teams, this takes less than a week.  After paperwork is signed, KYC is completed, and payment details are verified, we wire funds. This typically takes 1 to 2 weeks and happens before the program starts.        How is the program structured?            The program relies on 4 core activities: lectures, 1:1 mentorship, weekly check-ins and Demo Day.      Lectures:  We run weekly sessions where successful founders from our community share their stories and learnings as crypto operators, followed by a Q&A.      1:1 Mentorship:  Startups receive 1:1 mentorship from Alliance mentors. Discussions often revolve around product, go-to-market and fundraising. At times, mentors may also intro founders to experts within our network depending on the problem at hand.     Weekly Check-ins:  Founders share accomplishments and challenges with mentors every week to maintain accountability, momentum and gain insight on how to overcome potential blockers.     Demo Day:  6 weeks into the program companies start working on their narrative and pitch. Then, on week 10, startups meet select angels and VCs at Demo Day – both in-person, at the Alliance HQ in NYC, and online – and graduate from the program.      Each startup in our latest cohort received an average of over 50 intro requests after Demo Day from crypto's most value-add angels or funds, such as Paradigm, Multicoin and Dragonfly. Most startups also receive significant interest from clients or potential partners.        How is Alliance different from other accelerators?            The best people to answer this are founders who've done other programs before Alliance. Here's what they consistently tell us:     Cohorts are deliberately small (15-30 teams), which means mentors are truly hands-on. We get into the details of your product, your GTM, and your fundraise with you, everyday.    The peer support is something most founders say they didn't expect, but it ends up being one of the most valuable parts of Alliance.    And because we've been in the space since 2020, we're often one intro away from the exact customer, partner, or investor you need.         What are the next steps after I submit my application?            After you apply to the program, mentors will review your application within 1 week.  Our team will then invite ad hoc the most promising teams for an interview over Zoom. This will consist of a 10 minute fast-paced conversation with Alliance mentors (with guidelines shared before the interview).  Final decisions are then communicated over email within 24 to 48 hours.  Note that due to the sheer number of applications and interviews, mentors are unfortunately not able to give personalized feedback to teams that are not selected. You've seen Cursor sell to Elon for $60B . Maybe the previous generation was Mark Zuckerberg or Evan Spiegel. You look at these founders and compare yourself to them. EcoFund    Grant Program     Hackathon    Governance                                                                                                            EcoFund    Grant Program     Hackathon    Governance                                         MANTA Ecosystem Grant Program  Uncharted Seas Grants by Manta Pacific      Supercharge Your Growth  with Uncharted Seas Grants by Manta Pacific     Looking to take your business  to the next level?  The Manta Network Ecosystem Grant Program provides the resources needed to accelerate your growth and achieve significant results. Our goal is to foster innovation and support projects that bring value to the Manta Network ecosystem. We welcome applications from various sectors, including:          DEFI  Gaming  SocialFi  Infrastructure  AI       DEFI  Gaming  SocialFi  Infrastructure  AI       DEFI  Gaming  SocialFi  Infrastructure  AI         DePin  LRT/LST  ZK  MEME’s  NFT’s       DePin  LRT/LST  ZK  MEME’s  NFT’s       DePin  LRT/LST  ZK  MEME’s  NFT’s        Strategic Allocation:  Fueling Growth Across the Ecosystem  The $50 million EcoFund will be strategically distributed as follows:      Grants:   $10 Million     AI/DePIN, Zero-Knowledge, and Memes:  Emerging and dynamic sectors that hold immense potential to drive the industry forward.    General Grants:  We support a diverse range of initiatives through our general grants, fostering creativity and growth across the Manta ecosystem.         By providing grants support,  Manta Network aims to          Attract  promising new projects                Incentivize the development of innovative projects leveraging Manta Network's technology.            Expand  the Developer base                Support projects that provide utility and value to users, helping to attract and retain a loyal user base.            FOSTER  DEVELOPER GROWTH                Build a talent-centric developer community with robust tools and a user-friendly environment to accelerate innovation within the ecosystem.          Grant Eligibility  and Application Process  The Manta Network Ecosystem Grant Program operates on a rolling basis, meaning there are no designated application cohorts. Projects with innovative ideas and the potential to create value for the Manta ecosystem are encouraged to apply at any time.              $50,000  GRANT SIZE  The average grant amount awarded by the Manta Network Ecosystem Grant Program is upto $50,000, payable in either USDT or USDC.   Note: In certain instances, additional steps, such as KYB or KYC procedures, may be required based on the nature of the project and the discussions held with the Eco-fund team      Application   Submission   Complete and submit a formal application.     Initial   Review   The EcoFund team conducts an initial evaluation. If necessary, they will connect the project with relevant teams within Manta Network.     Approval   PROCESS    Grant applications undergo the following approval process:   Initial Grants Team Approval  The initial review by the EcoFund team determines whether the project qualifies for further consideration.    Core Team Approval  Promising projects are presented to the Manta Network core team for final approval.    Additional step  Grants exceeding $100,000 undergo final adjudication by the Manta Foundation.       grant   agreement   Once the project's KPIs, milestones, timeline, and other relevant details are finalized, a formal grant agreement will be drafted. This agreement outlines the terms and conditions of the grant and requires signatures from both Manta Network and the project team.     processing   timeframe   The grant application process typically takes up to two weeks post initial discussion.          Grant   Communication   and Project  Selection          post-application  communication                The Manta Network team will contact the project for further discussion after submission.            project  exclusivity                While exclusivity in building on Manta Network is not typically a requirement, the team welcomes in-depth discussions regarding milestones and key performance indicators (KPIs) after the initial communication.            project  prioritization                Projects committed to launching natively on Manta Network will receive preferential consideration and may be eligible for additional support.          Guide  for manta grants  Thank you for considering Uncharted Seas Grants by Manta Pacific. We are here to guide you from the deep ocean of the Pacific!             APPROVAL  Your grant application has been approved.  This means we'll be working together soon.    REFINEMENT NEEDED  Some applications need a bit more detail.  We'll provide suggestions to strengthen your proposal. This might involve setting clear goals (milestones) or adjusting the funding amount.    Reconsideration  In some cases, applications may not be approved right away.  This often happens if the proposal doesn’t fit right in the ecosystem for now. Once the project has achieved more milestones, we are happy to reconsider your application.          Categories  for the grants                1. Unleash the Power of  AI and DePIN Grants   The future of artificial intelligence (AI) and DePin is built on collaboration and innovation. DePIN and AI Grants offer you the chance to be at the forefront, pushing the boundaries of what's possible. Are you a developer passionate about the intersection of AI and DePin?             Apply for this Grant and unlock these transformative possibilities:     Revolutionize AI/DePIN Infrastructure   Develop robust and scalable foundations for AI/DePIN applications.    FUEl your vision   Overcome technical hurdles and bring your AI projects to life.    AI & DePIN Pioneer with Manta Network Marketing   Leverage Manta Network’s marketing support to become a leader in this emerging field.     $50,000  GRANT SIZE            2.  Be a ZK Trailblazer  with Manta Grants  Forge the future of zero-knowledge (ZK) blockchain applications with Manta Network’s ZK Grants.             Apply for this Grant and unlock these exciting opportunities:    Pioneer  ZK Innovation   Join a thriving community building the next generation of scalable and secure blockchain solutions. Manta Grants fuel your vision to push the boundaries of ZKP technology.    Elevate Your  Dev Toolkit   Gain access to cutting-edge resources and tools specifically designed for ZK development. Manta Grants can accelerate your workflow and empower you to build even more efficiently.    Build Real-World  ZK Apps   See your ideas come to life! Manta Grants can help you turn your ZK application into a reality, demonstrating its potential and influencing the future of blockchain.    AI & DePIN Pioneer with  Manta Marketing   Don't just build the future of ZK applications, with the help of Manta Network's zk Grants provide funding, marketing support, and ecosystem connections to fuel your project's growth and establish you as a pioneer in this transformative field. Apply now and join the Manta journey to shape the future of privacy-preserving blockchain.            3. Forge Your Blockchain Legacy: Dive into Innovation Grants!   Unlock the endless possibilities of blockchain with Innovation Grants. Perfect for developers with groundbreaking ideas in DeFi, Memes, Infrastructure, or other sectors.             Developer grants empower you to:    Fuel  Your Vision   Secure funding to bring your innovative projects to life.    Push  the Boundaries   Collaborate with a vibrant community to redefine blockchain technology.    Become a  Blockchain Pioneer   Gain recognition for your innovative work.    Don't miss this opportunity to shape the future! Apply for a developer grant today and join the forefront of blockchain innovation.          4. Moon Mission Grants: Memeing & Minting Your Way to the Top               Why Meme  grants      Community  Building  The memecoin era on Manta Pacific has begun, and now is the ideal time for projects to apply and lead the memecoin wave.    Unforeseen  Potential   Support projects with the potential to go viral and make a significant impact. Despite their playful origins, memecoins can evolve into ventures supporting charitable causes. Our grants aim to identify and nurture memecoins with similar potential for positive social impact.    Experimentation and  Innovation   Memecoin culture embraces experimentation and disruption. Create and develop unique applications within the space.      Criteria    Holder count 1,000 or more   This means there should be at least 1,000 unique holders of the asset.     Concentration   The top 100 holders should collectively own less than 60% of the total supply. This indicates a wider distribution of ownership and potentially less volatility.    Liquidity Minimum liquidity of $200,000   Liquidity refers to how easily an asset can be bought or sold on a marketplace. In this case, it means there should be at least $200,000 worth of trading activity readily available.    Liquidity providers 25 or more providers   This criterion looks for a healthy number of liquidity providers, which helps to ensure smooth buying and selling.    Lifespan More than 2 months   This indicates that the project has been around for a while and is not a flash in the pan.    Market cap $2 million or more   Market capitalization is the total value of all outstanding shares. A minimum market cap of $2 million suggests a certain level of establishment.    Trading volume Daily trading volume of $100,000 or more   This reflects active buying and selling of the asset, which can be a sign of interest and potential growth. Skip to main content                 Manta Network Docs     Manta Network  GitHub                                                                                                                                  On this page     Manta Pacific Ecosystem   The Manta Grants Program is designed to support projects that help Manta with activity, ecosystem growth, and Web3 & Web2 user acquisition, by using Manta’s frictionless user infrastructure and toolkits to bring Web3 decentralization and onboard large-scale Web2 applications onto Web3. Anyone who is building on Manta will have the chance to be funded by Manta Ecosystem Grant.  Explore all the applications and partners building on Manta:   https://manta.network/ecosystem.html    Building on Manta: What Manta Network Offers    A High-performance Blockchain for On-chain zk Applications  ​    The Fastest ZKPs  — Manta Network offers the fastest ZK-proving speed of any layer 1 blockchain, which offers an unrivaled user experience when it comes to on-chain zk applications.   Low Gas Cost  — Manta Network private transactions are just as inexpensive as an L2 transaction but performed on the L1 level, offering more decentralization.   Tools for Rapid Development Inside and Outside Web3  ​    Developer toolkits to make it easy to build and deploy applications  — Manta Network offers simple APIs and an SDK as well as plug-and-play services for zkNFTs/zkSBTs/MantaPay that give powerful and complete ZK features for developers to build on top of, without the need to understand ZK, cryptography or mathematics.   Multi-asset support  — Manta Network offers zk Applications-enhancing support for fungible (i.e., cryptocurrencies) and nonfungible (i.e., NFTs and SBTs) assets, enabling a rich variety of use cases including gamefi, socialfi, defi, web2 mobile applications, and more.   Less user friction  — Using Proof Keys developed by Manta Network, applications can support wallet-less experiences for private verifiability for users. In other words, the intimidating aspects of web3 can be abstracted entirely away from the users of web3 and web2.   Abstraction through applications and services  — Manta Network’s platforms including MantaPay, NPO, and Manta Name Service offer an intuitive user experience by relegating much of the complexities of ZK technology to the background. Leveraging these core platforms, developers can quickly ship prototypes and full products with out-of-the-box functionality enabling decentralized zk Applications.   A Web2 and Web3 Friendly Developer Experience  ​    Developer-friendly for mobile and non-web3 applications  — Manta Network’s APIs and SDKs are designed in a manner that provides a modular plug-and-play experience for mobile or desktop applications, inside and outside of web3. Developers do not have to build with web3 in mind from the ground up; rather, developers can take their applications (in whatever stage it’s at) and plug-in Manta Network’s functionality where it’s needed, to offer a decentralized user experience without impacting any development time or user experience changes.   Web 2.5 approach to attract non web3 users  — Using Proof Keys and the Manta API/SDKs, Manta Network enables a web 2.5 hybrid application experience, focusing on the best UX to onboard users that are unfamiliar with Web3. Unnecessarily complicated and intimidating aspects such as connecting wallets are abstracted away from the user, and they can focus more on deriving value from your application.   Additional Resources    Technical Resources  ​   As a project selected to participate in the Grants Program, you will have a direct line of communication with key members of our core engineering team. The team is there to help make your product a success; you are able to ask questions, get direct feedback, and address issues that require our support in a timely manner.   Funding Resources  ​   The Grants Program aims to fund innovative ideas for the entire Manta ecosystem, regardless of the infrastructure, SDKs, or applications. Developing more channels to support the growth of our ecosystem is one of our top goals. Beyond funding from the Grants Program, Manta Network will also provide resources to help take your project to the next level when it comes time to scale by introducing you to an extensive network of investors, partners, and other strategic contacts.   Marketing & Growth Resources  ​   Teams are welcome and encouraged to schedule weekly meetings with the Manta Network core team to consult on marketing and growth strategies. The Manta core team also invites projects for co-marketing campaigns that can quickly boost growth and exposure to a large, interested, and relevant audience within the Manta Network ecosystem.   Partnership Resources  ​   The Manta Team will support builders when reaching out to external parties for partnerships and promotional opportunities so that they can best position themselves to grow their brand.   Guidelines for Grant Categories   We encourage any projects in the web2 or web3 space that are exploring components of decentralized on-chain zk Applications with no impact on user experience to apply for a Manta Ecosystem Grant. We look forward to supporting you in various ways that can lead to a successful outcome for your project. At the current stage of the Manta Network ecosystem, we are particularly interested in projects falling under the following categories:   SocialFi Mobile Applications  GameFi Mobile Applications  Bridging Solutions  zk Applications-oriented DeFi solutions    Manta Grants Application Process    Submit Application  ​   Please  submit the application  for the grant, and provide as much detail as possible.   Application Review & Team Presentation  ​   The Manta Team will review all applications on a rolling basis, and reach out to selected applicants on the next steps. If necessary, we may request additional information. This screening process typically takes two weeks.   Second Round of Review  ​   The applications will be further reviewed by the community committee consisting of select members from our official team and VCs and community members to explore the project, concept, and grant request. The committee will then determine the projects that proceed to the voting process.   Implementation & Follow up  ​   We will have a bi-weekly follow-up call to help the team with technical and other forms of support. added: TheDAO Security Fund | Initiatives                                                                                                                           TheDAO   Security Fund      Initiatives  Suggest an initiative          Connect wallet                  Ecosystem-funded security initiatives  $ 247,852   raised for  Ethereum security  initiatives     Security initiatives looking for funding             Show top matches            +  Suggest an initiative  Know something the ecosystem should fund? Pitch it.    Grant  Source-Level Debugging for Solidity: ethdebug in solc  solc does not emit the debug information debuggers need, so every tool reverse-engineers compiler behavior and breaks when the compiler changes. This funds implementing the ethdebug format directly in solc, with debug data that survives the full optimizer pipeline so it works on production builds.         $151,008   of $279,000 · 3 backers   54.1%    Donate  Details          Pledged by         Grant  End-to-End Formally Verified Vyper Compiler  This grant funds a machine-checked proof that Vyper compilation preserves the meaning of source programs, plus the infrastructure to re-verify supported releases. It brings abstract methods, unbounded dynamic arrays and storage packing into the verified pipeline. The intended result is a public verified compilation mode, available through the official compiler as `--verified`, with documented guarantees and production adoption.         $100,025   of $600,000 · 4 backers   16.7%    Donate  Details          Pledged by       RFP  Wallet Security for Post-Quantum Ethereum  Post-quantum Ethereum needs wallet support and signer safety alongside protocol upgrades. This RFP funds independent security-proof research, a shared signer safety profile, and public signer and verifier tests. It covers hardware and browser compatibility, frame transactions, scalability, hash functions, and builder and user guidance on signature budgets. Adoption requires public tests, conformance statements, and support from wallet suppliers.         $553.70   of $250,000 · 3 backers   0.2%    Donate  Details            Grant  LeekWallet: an open DIY hardware wallet with a secure element PIN gate, and build workshops in Mexico  LeekWallet is an open source hardware wallet anyone can build from about $30 of parts bought from any seller, whose device decodes every transaction itself and refuses what it cannot display. This grant adds an ATECC608B secure element that keeps the PIN attempt counter in silicon the main chip cannot rewrite, closing the project's largest open weakness. It then puts at least 80 working devices in builders' hands through one in-person workshop in Mexico City and one online workshop, with build guides in English and Spanish for first-time and experienced solderers.         $87.15   of $32,190 · 2 backers   0.3%    Donate  Details            Grant  thatsRekt: EVM exploit alerts for the public good.  thatsRekt aggregates and reads trusted security accounts on X, uses AI to work out which posts are actually about a live exploit, and turns the good ones into structured, on-chain alerts that anyone can read for free. This grant pays for a better AI/ML detection pipeline, build an open API and automated X posting so the feed actually reaches third party integrators and other tools, plus two more guardian teams running their own detectors so the network isn't dependent on one team.         $4.99   of $45,000 · 1 backer   0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  Decentralized, Privacy-Preserving EDR  Endpoint Detection and Response is one of the highest-value security controls a team can run, and almost nobody in crypto runs it, because mainstream EDR sits in your kernel and streams telemetry to a central vendor. This grant funds an EDR crypto teams will actually adopt, user-space, self-hostable, privacy-preserving by construction, tuned for Web3 threats. Auditware is the recipient.         $1.29   of $300,000 · 1 backer   0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  Towards a Formally Verified Solc  Solc compiles the overwhelming majority of contracts deployed on Ethereum as well as its rollups and underpins [99% of Ethereum’s value](https://www.growthepie.com/quick-bites/compiler-tvs) on-chain which makes security the highest priority. A correctness defect in the compiler itself can silently undermine every audit performed on the source code it processes.
The Solidity team is working towards a formally verified compiler with two focused and clearly bounded projects to verify key parts of the solc compilation chain:
1. Formalization + Agent Based Optimization Harness for the Solc Stack Shuffler
2. Formalization of the semantics of Core Solidity

Both of the projects are of independent interest as standalone projects, but they would also be key building blocks in any future effort to produce a full end to end verification chain for solc.         $0   of $350,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  Safe Lockdown Guard: An Emergency Freeze for Kidnapping and Coercion  Kidnapping and physical coercion can force Safe owners to authorize transfers with perfectly valid signatures. Safe Lockdown Guard gives them a separate emergency action: freeze guarded transfers with a credential that cannot spend funds. Runtime Capital has built and published the open-source audit candidate; this $14,000 request funds the remaining independent audit cost, with a final milestone tied to verified use on Ethereum mainnet. The audit, fixes and installation documentation will be public for every compatible Safe operator.         $0   of $14,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  DPRK IT Worker Screening for the Ethereum Ecosystem  NorthScan will provide approved Ethereum organizations with a controlled service for screening GitHub profiles for behavioral, identity and network signals associated with DPRK IT worker activity. The six-month pilot will combine automated assessments with selected human review, practical integration resources and measurable adoption across the ecosystem. The grant will also validate a sustainable freemium and paid-access model for trusted organizations.         $0   of $50,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  NanoJS Investigations: Sustaining Independent Ethereum Forensic Casework and Open Tooling  NanoJS Investigations funds continued independent forensic investigation into Ethereum exploits, alongside NanoJS Pipeline, an open-source toolkit for sanctions screening, wallet clustering, and contract discovery. Nine investigations published to date have led to confirmed exchange freezes and law-enforcement filings. This grant sustains casework already in progress and opens the pipeline for other investigators to use.         $0   of $10,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  Self-serve scoped permissions and pre-signature checks for Safes and AI agents  Self-custody fails at the moment of signing. This grant builds a self-serve app that turns on audited Zodiac controls with safe defaults, adds the pre-signature checks that do not exist yet, and scopes an AI agent so it holds no key. Apache 2.0 throughout. The largest milestone pays only when 100 Safes outside Protocol Wealth run it holding at least $20,000,000, verifiable onchain.         $0   of $135,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  Onchain Risk Map: An Open Operational Incident Graph for Ethereum Security  Onchain Risk Map converts documented security incidents into reusable evidence for
Ethereum builders. It maps failures across software delivery, wallets, signing, account
authorization, infrastructure, and execution using typed relationships and explicit
evidence confidence.
This grant will fund an open, versioned Ethereum dataset with at least 30 independently
reviewed incidents, 30 defensive-control assessments, and tools for comparing failures.
External use will be documented through public work products from at least six

organizations.         $0   of $50,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  Exploit Exposure Layer: Free Data on Every Wallet Still Approved to an Exploited Contract  After an exploit, the token approvals users granted to the exploited contract stay live and keep getting drained, sometimes for years. Revoke.cash will scan every supported chain for every contract on its public exploit list, compute which wallets are still exposed, and serve that data through a free API so any wallet or explorer can warn its own users. The multichain exploit check on Revoke.cash moves out of the paid tier and becomes free, and a public metrics page tracks exposure, revocations, and value at risk per exploit.         $0   of $100,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  TEE Security Handbook: practical verification, failure analysis and recovery for Ethereum  Expand Bluethroat Labs' existing TEE Security Handbook with four reviewed engineering chapters, reusable security checklists and runnable examples. The work covers attestation verification, malicious-host interfaces, state recovery, and verification from source code to deployment. Funding also supports maintenance and documented use by independent Ethereum-facing teams.         $0   of $18,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  From Community Contracts to OpenZeppelin Contracts: ERC-7540 Asynchronous Vaults  OpenZeppelin Community Contracts is where OpenZeppelin and ecosystem teams build implementations of new standards before they enter OpenZeppelin Contracts, the trusted library Ethereum projects import. The ERC-7540 asynchronous vault suite, built with the Tokenized Vault Foundation and Centrifuge, is now complete but unaudited. This grant funds its audit, the fixes, the published report and its release in OpenZeppelin Contracts, so every tokenized fund, real-world asset pool and staking vault can build on it securely.         $0   of $90,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  Ethereum Decompiler Benchmark & Open Bytecode Analysis Standard  Build a public EVM decompiler benchmark and an open, vendor-neutral API/CLI specification for bytecode analysis. ExVul will serve as the first reference implementation, while the benchmark and specification are designed for independent use by other decompilers and security tools. The project also includes a $40,000 adoption milestone tied to publicly verifiable external use.         $0   of $120,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            RFP  Spec Bank: a public, composable registry of formal specifications for DeFi  DeFi protocols compose like Lego, but an understanding of what a protocol actually guarantees rarely travels with it, and the problem only gets worse as new systems integrate old ones. Spec Bank tests whether a public, permissionless registry can fix that: a protocol's formal model, called a spec, gets uploaded once, and afterward anyone can submit an invariant, a specific property, and have it proved or disproved against that spec automatically and in public. Invariants can build on other specs the way the protocols themselves do, so a downstream integrator can prove a property like "no loss of principal" by citing an upstream protocol's spec directly. This RFP funds a proof of concept testing whether that crowdsourcing mechanic actually works, with governance kept deliberately thin: specs and invariants that are correct and useful attract reuse, rather than needing a central body to debate their acceptance.         $0   of $100,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  Fund Echidna Development Through 2027  Fund Gustavo Grieco, Echidna's creator and maintainer, to carry out Echidna's 2026 to 2027 roadmap during 2027: keep EVM execution current, improve campaign and worker architecture, strengthen symbolic verification, turn agent control into a dependable workflow and optimize execution performance. At minimum, the period produces three tagged maintenance or minor releases, at least two substantial roadmap outcomes delivered in tagged releases, three technical posts, and a public SKILL prompt and MCP workflow for AI agents.         $0   of $48,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  Open EVM Compiler Differential Fuzzing Platform  Every EVM contract is only as correct as the compiler that built it, and no contract audit catches a compiler bug. This grant turns a working prototype differential fuzzer into a maintained open source platform, then pays mainly for getting compiler teams to run it themselves. It already produced confirmed findings in solx, Sonatina and Plank. Nearly half the money pays only when named compiler teams run it against their own compilers, in their own CI.         $0   of $75,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  Account Abstraction and Mempool Security Analytics  EIPsInsight already tracks Ethereum standards, governance, upgrades, and on-chain usage in the open, including early mempool and MEV security signals.

EIPsInsight becomes an open security-visibility layer for Ethereum account abstraction and mempool risk analysis. This $45,000 grant funds a 3-month build of the security and network analytics infrastructure, centered on account abstraction with targeted mempool and MEV intelligence, plus a dedicated adoption milestone proven over a longer window of up to 12 months.

Account-abstraction focus (EIP-4337, EIP-7702, EIP-8141): cross-chain indexing, EntryPoint and set-code usage metrics, typed-transaction migration trends, gas economics, and threat watchlists for malicious sweeper contracts post-Pectra.

Mempool and MEV: post-Dencun analytics tracking sandwich attacks, extracted value in USD, block-level sandwiching rate, and customizable threat alerts.Account Abstraction and Mempool Security Analytics         $0   of $45,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  Colibri — Production Infrastructure and Ecosystem Adoption for Trustless Ethereum Access  This grant takes Colibri, a trustless stateless Ethereum client, from production-ready core to ecosystem-wide adoption in a single combined program. It funds hardening of the verification core, Pragmatic Adaptive Privacy, a verified transaction-security foundation, multi-chain expansion with a verification fallback, Go/C++ developer bindings, and a large-scale adoption push targeting at least 30 real application integrations, including 8 from a named list of high-value targets.         $0   of $640,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  The Ethernaut: Six New Levels Built from Real-World Exploits  The Ethernaut is OpenZeppelin's open-source wargame where developers learn smart contract security by exploiting real flaws, level by level. First delivered in 2017, The Ethernaut has been the first blockchain security experience for many devs and auditors in the space, and we strive every year to add new relevant exploits to it. This grant funds six new levels built from recent real-world exploits and published audit findings, reviewed and live on ethernaut.openzeppelin.com within 2 months.         $0   of $44,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  Open Standard and Automated Triage Tooling for Ethereum Security Issues  AI-assisted reporting has made security submissions cheap to write and expensive to check. This grant funds an open standard for deterministic proofs-of-concept (PoC), plus tooling that replays a submitted PoC, records a source-level trace, and flags invalid assumptions and bogus preconditions. Triagers get a faster way to tell a valid PoC from one that only fires inside a rigged test setup. Reporters get a way to build PoCs that hold up under real-world assumptions before they submit.         $0   of $150,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  Securing Ethereum with Formal Verification  AI is making it faster to attack software, giving attackers a meaningful edge. Formal verification is widely considered the strongest security guarantee in software correctness. This grant aims to increase formal verification adoption across the Ethereum ecosystem with TVL secured as its main success metric.         $0   of $200,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            RFP  Provider-Independent, Client-Verified ENS Resolution  Today a wallet or gateway resolves an ENS name with one call to one RPC provider and trusts the answer; the correct record is on the chain and nothing checks it. This RFP suggests a library that asks two independent sources, verifies against a block header, and flags disagreement, plus a public test suite that any .eth gateway operator can run to prove they resolve and serve names correctly, so more than one company can serve .eth sites. It is anchored on the April 2026 eth.limo registrar hijack, where one operator's DNSSEC setup was the only thing between 2 million .eth sites and phishing pages. Half the budget pays only on adoption by named wallets, dapps, and gateway operators.         $0   of $150,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            RFP  Production-Ready Local-First Safe UI  This RFP funds a production-ready, local-first Safe multisig UI, deployed to IPFS with reproducible builds, that anyone can run with nothing but an RPC endpoint and a wallet. It is an independent way to execute transactions if Safe for any reason becomes unreachable, and a tool to cross-check every hash before signers approve.         $0   of $120,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  ForensIQ: Faster Ethereum Incident Response Through Evidence Reconstruction  ForensIQ is building an open-source module that connects off-chain incident evidence (logs, files, transaction hashes) with Ethereum activity to reconstruct attack timelines, trace fund flows, and flag transfers to attributed exchange addresses. It replaces the manual handoffs between logs, block explorers, and attribution tools with one evidence-linked workflow that produces a verified response package faster. The grant funds the missing connective layer on top of ForensIQ's existing MVP (case management, Crystal and Etherscan integrations), not a rebuild of the platform. Success is measured through pilots with protocol, exchange, and law-enforcement investigators, tracking time to a verified timeline and correctness rather than a promised percentage improvement.         $0   of $135,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            RFP  Directory of Value  Before a security researcher can analyze a protocol, they have to find it, and today there is no neutral way to enumerate the contracts that actually hold value. Directory of Value is a permissionless registry where anyone can identify a contract as valuable, plus an open indexing layer that exposes every entry as data a researcher or an automated agent can query in full. It records identification without imposing judgment, and no single gatekeeper decides who appears. This RFP funds the specification, implementation, audit, deployment, and adoption of that directory.         $0   of $185,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            RFP  Community Fuzzing Tooling for Ethereum Ecosystem Projects  The Ethereum ecosystem is lacking a solution for scalable, continuous, and compute-intensive fuzzing campaigns for projects. For each project to subscribe to their own solution would be costly and could have diminishing returns over time to make it a worthwhile investment of time, money, and human capital. We are requesting proposals from applicants who have developed or can develop tools to orchestrate fuzzing at scale, assign compute resources efficiently, and flex these resources up and down in an agile manner so that any team can orchestrate their own fuzzing campaign for themselves. A self-serve model. This RFP would fund the construction and maintenance of such a tool.         $0   of $150,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  A Unified Platform for Web3 OpSec  Web3 OpSec tooling is fragmented. Frameworks, trainings, scanners and breach monitoring all exist, but they live in separate places and nobody has a single view of where they stand. This grant funds one platform that pulls them together into a task list with owners and statuses, so a team can see its posture and what to fix next. Auditware is the recipient: they've already built the foundation, and this opens it up to the ecosystem as a public good and funds its development into an impactful and full-featured platform.         $0   of $250,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            RFP  OPSEC Ratings Coalition to Build & Maintain an "L2Beat for OPSEC"  Fund a single coordinator to bring at least six OPSEC auditing firms together around one industry-agreed rating standard: an A / AA / AAA tier a team earns and renews yearly, with a six-month check-in and automatic suspension when its security posture changes. The firms already running OPSEC audits become the accredited raters, apply one shared scoring template inside their existing flow and publish tiers only, never a team's report or score. Rated teams pay a fixed fee into a membership body that owns the standard and the board once the coordinator hands off. A simple public board shows who is rated; teams with unacceptable OPSEC simply don't appear.         $0   of $150,000  0.0%    Donate  Details            Grant  Automated EIP Compliance Checks for Ethereum Clients  Ethereum's client teams implement EIPs by reading specification text and writing code, and conformance test suites only catch the divergences somebody thought to write a test for. PRSpec uses LLM analysis to compare EIP specification text directly against client source code and flag semantic mismatches, and it has already surfaced a real cross-client inconsistency in how EIP-1559's base-fee burn is implemented. This grant funds turning it from a research tool into a self-hosted pre-release check running in the staging pipelines of the major execution clients.         $0   of $20,000  0.0%    Donate  Details              Want to pledge support?
